newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 25.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

News Corp announced in London on Thursday that it planned to sell US$1 billion of preferred securities for the purchase of stock in its 40-percent-owned BSkyB. Under the plan, institutional investors could purchase securities and warrants to buy ordinary shares or American Depositary Shares (ADSs) in the satellite broadcaster. News Corp's plan hit BSkyB's stock, which fell 28.5 pence to 607.5 in heavy morning trade. News' ADRs fell 1/8 to 22-3/4 overnight in New York.

Seven Network Ltd Chairman Kerry Stokes said on Thursday that if it were successful in its legal action against other shareholders in Optus Vision it would probably exercise its option in that outcome to buy out the other shareholders in the pay television operator.

Shares in mining group RTZ Corp Plc were indicated higher in London overnight after Anglo-Australian company RTZ-CRA said that third quarter production was up on last year in almost all of its products. The shares jumped 6-1/2p to 971-1/2p by 0710 GMT in pre-market trade shortly after the announcement.

Newcrest Mining Ltd said late on Thursday that it achieved an abnormal profit of A$270.0 million from the closeout of gold hedge positions in its first financial quarter. It also posted an A$154.0 million net profit for the first quarter after the abnormal profit. Newcrest's Managing Director John Quinn also told the company's annual meeting it would increase production from its Telfer mine in Western Australia over the next two years to nearly 600,000 ounces of gold a year.

Highlands Gold Ltd said late on Thursday that pre-feasability studies at the group's Ramu and Frieda River projects in Papua New Guinea had shown both could be developed into viable mines within a decade.
